A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RE-Bench study and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–I. Text and rendered-page comparisons support a reliable assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations across seven environments, including 71 attempts by 61 human experts and experiments with Claude 3.5 Sonnet and o1-preview.

after.justification: v2 retains the original human and AI-agent experiments, quantitative performance results, and empirical appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The benchmark design, scoring procedures, Modular and AIDE scaffolds, and reference-solution procedures remain unchanged. Revised code-length statistics and a shortened scaffold label do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven research-engineering environments and retain the same datasets, task requirements, and human population. Appendix C contains unchanged environment descriptions.

E2.justification: The human comparisons, two Claude 3.5 Sonnet versions, o1-preview, and their Modular/AIDE configurations remain unchanged. Removing 'general-duet' from Figure 14's heading does not remove the illustrated agent or comparison.

E3.justification: The reported time budgets, data splits, scoring normalization, best-of-k procedures, and experimental settings remain unchanged in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–C. Revised summary values do not document a changed evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 10 revises the existing analysis of engineering complexity versus the human–AI performance gap, changing both code-size coordinates and performance ratios. The analysis retains its question and broad negative association; appendix case studies and supplementary analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Repeated-run information, percentile-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, and starting-score variability reporting are unchanged. Neither version adds a different uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 10 changes reported agent/human ratios: approximately 1.15 to 0.98 for Optimize a Kernel, 0.79 to 0.83 for Finetune GPT-2 for QA, and 0.38 to 0.42 for Optimize LLM Foundry. The kernel point crosses parity. Table 3 also revises three code-length values; other performance figures and appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The score-normalization equation and mathematical task/scoring definitions in Section 3.2.2 and Appendix C are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution and central findings: agents progress faster initially, while humans benefit more from longer time budgets. The Figure 10 revisions do not produce revised core claims.

C2.justification: Sections 5–6 retain the same explanations of agent successes and failures and the same limitations concerning representativeness, noise, overfitting, cost, and scaffolding. Figure 10's discussion remains unchanged despite its revised values.

D1.justification: Table 3 revises documented code lengths: Optimize a Kernel 180 to 218, Optimize LLM Foundry 1,651 to 1,392, and Finetune GPT-2 for QA 647 to 716. Figure 14 removes the 'general-duet' identifier. These are documentation changes; implementation instructions, hardware details, and resource-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 59 references, related-work discussion, benchmark comparison table, and research positioning are retained. Reference-page reflow introduces no new cited work.

P1.justification: v2 adds Holden Karnofsky and an affiliation footnote, introduces acknowledgements, and makes small wording and capitalization edits. The scientific narrative and section organization are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Figure 10 is redrawn with revised axis ranges and point placements, and Figure 14's heading is shortened. Authorship and acknowledgement additions cause limited text and reference reflow; the figure and table inventory is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 expands contributor credit, but the PDFs do not establish whether the revised Figure 10 ratios improve accuracy. It also introduces a numerical inconsistency: Table 3's largest code size becomes 1,392, while Table 7 retains 1,651. With the benefit of the numerical revisions unresolved and this reporting defect, the net quality direction is uncertain.
